title: 'JUSTICE FOR MACHUAR': Local South Sudanese community rally at police headquarters
article: Around 100 people rallied in front of the Winnipeg Police headquarters including members of the city's South Sudanese community on Friday to demand answers after Machuar Mawien Madut was fatally shot by Winnipeg Police on Saturday morning at his suite in an apartment building on Colony Street near Broadway.

Carrying signs and chanting "Justice for Machuar" and other slogans, the protestors presented a list of six demands including that the officers involved in the shooting be identified and charged and for more funding for mental health intervention programs. They also demanded an apology from WPS for portraying the 43-year-old father-of-three as a criminal who was attempting to break into his own suite and was shot in his own apartment.

Many of the protestors wore t-shirts with Madut's picture and the words, "A mental health intervention not a bullet." Madut, who came to Winnipeg as a refugee from South Sudan in 2003, was suffering mental health issues after the breakup of his marriage.

"People who are suffering with mental health or living with mental health (issues) should not be shot," said community activist Sandy Deng, who led the rally. "They should be helped. They should be given intervention. If the appropriate action was taken he wouldn't be dead today."

"He immigrated to Canada from war-torn South Sudan to find peace, not to face bullets," said Margaret Yanga, treasurer of the Council of South Sudanese Communities of Manitoba which organized the rally.

While unable to discuss specifics since it is being investigated by the Independent Investigation Unit of Manitoba (IIU), a police spokesperson said the WPS has reached out to the South Sudanese community.

"They now have an understanding of how our processes work (but) we still unfortunately cannot give them answers to how that incident unfolded," said Const. Tammy Skrabek. "But we've assured them that they will get those answers once the investigation is complete."
Despite the community's outrage, Skrabek said the WPS is attempting to keep lines of communications open.
"They know that at any time if they have any other questions regarding this, they are welcome to come back to the police service and we will share information as best as we can," said Skrabek.

"They just came to us to talk about how to do this protest in a safe way for everyone," said Deng, who had no comment on relations between the community and police. "So we didn't discuss anything specific about the case."

During Friday's rally, the Council of South Sudanese Communities of Manitoba made six demands:
- Name of officer(s) involved in the shooting of Machuar Madut and charges to be laid.
- Full report and investigation into the events that happened on Saturday, Feb. 23 from the Winnipeg Police Service and the Independent Investigation Unit of Manitoba.
- Implementation of community focused interventions and appropriate response for persons experiencing multiple barriers, such as limited language skills or coming from refugee/immigrant background.
- An apology from WPS for portraying Machuar Madut as a criminal who was attempting a break and enter, when he lived in the building and was shot in his own apartment.
- More funding to mental health intervention programs and hiring more trained mental health staff.
- Support and resources for Madut's family.
